candidateFields.source:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.

candidateFields.source:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
candidateFields.currentTarget:
Letamo kapa letangwana le ka boloka metsi a phallang, empa bongata bo fumanehang bo itshetlehile ka pula ya sebaka seo, sebaka se kgoboketsang metsi (catchment), tahlehelo le hore na o sebedisa metsi a makae.

Dihla tsa pula di fapana ho pholletsa le Afrika Borwa (South Africa). Sebedisa ditlaleho tsa sebaka seo mme o rale bakeng sa dry periods; letamo le tletseng ha le a tiisetswa.

Pele o fetola tsela ya noka kapa molatswana (watercourse) kapa o haha meaho ya polokelo, hlahloba tumello e hlokahalang le balaodi ba metsi.

Letamo le hloka dipatlisiso tsa setsha le moralo o entsweng ke motho ya nang le ditshwaneleho tse loketseng. Metsi a phallang ho tswa sebakeng sa pokellelo (catchment runoff), mobu, metheo, kotsi e ka tlase (downstream risk) le tsela e bolokehileng ya metsi a tletseng (safe spillway) kaofela a bohlokwa.

O se ke wa nka hore pula ya selemo le selemo e o jwetsa boholo ba morwallo kapa polokelo eo o tla ba le yona.

Phallo e sa laolweng ya metsi a tletseng e ka kgohola le ho pshatla lerako. Rala tsela e bolokehileng bakeng sa metsi a feteletseng pele ho kaho.

Metsi a ka lahleha ka evaporation and seepage. Hlahloba boemo ba metsi mme o batle dibaka tse dutlang kapa kgoholeho.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. O se ke wa jala difate hodima lerako la letamo la mobu.

Diphoofolo di ka senya mabopo mme tsa eketsa mantle ka hara metsi. Ho ba teng ha tsona ha ho etse hore metsi a hlweke kapa a bolokehe.

candidateFields.source:
Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
candidateFields.currentTarget:
Marulelo a hao a ka bokella metsi a pula. Bongata bo itshetlehile ka boholo ba marulelo, pula le tahlehelo.

Hlahloba hore na thepa ya marulelo e loketse ho bokella metsi a pula pele o hokela tanka.

Sebedisa boholo ba marulelo jwalo ka ha bo bonwa ho tloha hodimo le ditlaleho tsa pula ya sebaka seo. Ebe o dumella metsi a fosang koto, a kgelohang kapa a kgaphatsehang ha tanka e tletse.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Bapisa phepelo le tshebediso eo o e rerileng.

Metsi a theohang marulelong a ka nka lerole, mantle le tshilafalo e nngwe. Sekgelo sa ho qala ha phallo (first-flush diverter) se boloka karolo e nngwe ya metsi a pele a phallang kantle ho tanka.

Bongata bo hlokahalang ba ho kgeloha bo itshetlehile ka marulelo le tsamaiso. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

Sekgelo (diverter) ha se etse hore metsi a setseng a bolokehele ho nowa.

Boholo ba tanka bo itshetlehile ka tlhoko ya metsi, pula, boholo ba marulelo le the length of dry periods.

Ngola tshebediso e rerilweng mme o hakanye tlhoko ya yona ho tswa ditlalehong tsa hao. Bapisa seo le phepelo ho pholletsa le dihla.

Rala seo o tla se etsa ha metsi a bolokilweng a qala ho fela. Lebitso la provense feela le ke ke la o jwetsa boholo ba tanka eo o e hlokang.

Boloka tanka e kwahetswe, screen openings against insects, mme o hlokomele marulelo, dikoto le sekgelo (diverter). Boloka metsi a pula a arohane le diphaephe tsa metsi a nowang.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka diteko le kalafo tse loketseng tshebediso e rerilweng.

Sefa sa mantlha feela hase tiiso ya metsi a nowang. Metsi a sebediswang dijalong tsa dijo le ona a hloka tlhahlobo ya polokeho.

candidateFields.source:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.

candidateFields.source:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.

A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.

candidateFields.source:
Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

candidateFields.source:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.

candidateFields.source:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.

Muxaka wun'we wa xisele (swale) i mugodi wo leha lowu ringaneke, lowu celiweke eka khanthura. Swisele swin'wana swi dizayiniwa swi rhelela katsongo hi ndlela leyi lawulekaka, leswaku swi yisa mati lama taleke hi ku nonoka eka ndhawu leyi hlayisekeke yo huma. Ndlela leyi faneleke ndhawu ya wena yi titshege hi misava, ku rhelela, ku humesa mati na ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze. Kombela mutsundzuxi wa laha kaya loyi a leteriweke leswaku a kambela layini, ndlela ya mati lama taleke na ndhawu leyi ma yaka kona u nga si cela.

Kombela mutsundzuxi wa laha kaya loyi a leteriweke leswaku a kambela misava, ku rhelela na ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze. Xifaniso a hi dizayini yo aka ha yona.

Ku rhelela ntsena a ku ku byeli loko xisele xi fanerile. Misava, ku humesa mati, misava leyi nga tiyangiki na mati lama taka hi le henhla ka ndhawu yo rhelela hinkwaswo swa nkoka.

Hlayisa misava yi funengetekile kahle. Kuma nkambelo wa laha kaya u nga si cela eka steep, wet or unstable land. Mindzilakano ya byanyi (grass barriers) na titerasi (terraces) na swona swi lava dizayini leyi faneleke ndhawu.

candidateFields.source:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.

candidateFields.source:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.
candidateFields.currentTarget:
Mati lama tirhisiweke ekaya ma nga va na germs, salts, cleaning products ni other substances. Swiletelo a swi hlamuseli swihlovo hinkwaswo hi ndlela yin’we. Swiletelo swa Afrika-Dzonga swa hambana hi mati ya le khixini ni mati yo hlantswa swiambalo.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

Xifaniso xa ntolovelo a hi pulani ya purasi. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.
candidateFields.proposedTarget:
Mati lama tirhisiweke ekaya ma nga va na germs, salts, cleaning products ni swilo swin’wana. Swiletelo a swi hlamuseli swihlovo hinkwato hi ndlela yin’we. Swiletelo swa Afrika-Dzonga swi hambana hi mati ya le khixini ni mati yo hlantswa swiambalo.

U nga katsi mati ya toilet, mati yo huma eka nappies, mati yo hlantswa munhu loyi a vabyaka kumbe mati yo hlantswa swiharhi eka reuse plan. U nga tirhisi nakambe mati lama nga na harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, kombela municipality na qualified local sanitation adviser ku kambela source leyi kongomeke, vukorhokeri bya mati na sanitation bya household, intended use na site. Loko ndzayo leyi yi nga kumeki kumbe yi nga ri erivaleni, u nga ma tirhisi nakambe.

A generic picture a hi pulani ya purasi. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep wastewater away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

Loko reuse system yi ri karhi yi tirha naswona mati ma nunha, ma yima kumbe ma onha swimilana, tshika ku ma tirhisa kutani u lava ndzayo ya qualified local adviser.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Mofuta o mong wa swale ke level trench on contour. E fokotsa lebelo mme e hasanya runoff, hore metsi a mang a kgone ho kenella mobung o loketseng. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Mokgwa o loketseng naha ya hao o itshetlehile ka mobu, slope, drainage le storm flow. Pele o tjheka, trained local adviser a hlahlobe line, overflow le receiving point.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Mofuta o mong wa swale ke a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Mokgwa o loketseng naha ya hao o itshetlehile ka mobu, slope, drainage le storm flow. Pele o tjheka, kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe line, overflow le receiving point.
changedSegments.amendmentReason: High-risk construction geometry is source-exact for level trench on contour, controlled grade, excess water, safe outlet, line, overflow, receiving point and before-digging assessment. Ordinary land-fit explanation and local adviser framing remain localized; no long trench is added.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Mobu o epolotsweng o etsa berm on the downhill side; moo difate di ka jalwang ha site design e loketse.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Mobu o epolotsweng o etsa berm ka lehlakoreng le theohelang, moo difate di ka jalwang teng ha site design e loketse.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Difate tse jetsweng moo di ka nka moisture e bolokilweng mobung ka mora pula, ho ya ka site.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Difate tse jalwang moo di ka sebedisa metsi a bolokilweng mobung ka mora pula, ho ya ka site.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rera safe overflow pele o tjheka.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rala tsela e bolokehileng ya overflow pele o tjheka.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Route eo ha e a tshwanela ho senya slope ka erosion kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. Downstream swale kapa dam e lokela ho kgona ho amohela metsi ao ka polokeho.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Tsela ha e a lokela ho baka erosion moepeng kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe mobu, slope le storm flow. Setshwantsho ha se construction design.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe mobu, slope le storm flow. Setshwantsho hase construction design.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Slope feela ha e bolele hore swale e a lokela. Soil, drainage, unstable ground le metsi a tswang upslope kaofela di bohlokwa.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Slope feela ha e bolele hore swale e loketse. Soil, drainage, unstable ground le metsi a tswang upslope kaofela di bohlokwa.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Boloka ground cover e ntle. Fumana local assessment pele o tjheka mobung o steep, wet kapa unstable. Grass barriers le terraces le tsona di hloka design e loketseng site.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Boloka ground cover e ntle. Fumana local assessment pele o tjheka sebakeng se steep, wet kapa unstable. Grass barriers le terraces le tsona di hloka design e loketseng site.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Metsi a ka lahleha ka evaporation and seepage. Hlahloba boemo ba metsi mme o batle dibaka tse dutlang kapa kgoholeho.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Metsi a ka lahleha ka evaporation le seepage. Hlahloba boemo ba metsi mme o batle dibaka tse dutlang kapa kgoholeho.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. O se ke wa jala difate hodima lerako la letamo la mobu.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Boloka spillway e sa thibehang mme o hlokomele bank cover e boletsweng design. O se ke wa jala difate hodima lerako la earth dam.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Sebedisa boholo ba marulelo jwalo ka ha bo bonwa ho tloha hodimo le ditlaleho tsa pula ya sebaka seo. Ebe o dumella metsi a fosang koto, a kgelohang kapa a kgaphatsehang ha tanka e tletse.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Sebedisa boholo ba marulelo jwalo ka ha bo bonwa ho tloha hodimo le ditlaleho tsa pula ya sebaka seo. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.
changedSegments.currentSegment: An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Bapisa phepelo le tshebediso eo o e rerileng.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Palo ya pula ya selemo kaofela ha e o bolelle hore na metsi a makae a tla fumaneha nakong ya dry spell. Bapisa phepelo le ditshebediso tseo o di rerileng.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Metsi a theohang marulelong a ka nka lerole, mantle le tshilafalo e nngwe. Sekgelo sa ho qala ha phallo (first-flush diverter) se boloka karolo e nngwe ya metsi a pele a phallang kantle ho tanka.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Metsi a theohang marulelong a ka nka lerole, mantle le tshilafalo e nngwe. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Bongata bo hlokahalang ba ho kgeloha bo itshetlehile ka marulelo le tsamaiso. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Bongata bo lokelang ho kgeloswa bo itshetlehile ka marulelo le system. Latela ditaelo tsa supplier tsa sizing le maintenance; ha ho volume e le nngwe bakeng sa marulelo ohle.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Boholo ba tanka bo itshetlehile ka tlhoko ya metsi, pula, boholo ba marulelo le the length of dry periods.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Boholo ba tank bo itshetlehile ka tlhoko ya metsi, pula, sebaka sa marulelo le bolelele ba dry periods.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Ngola tshebediso e rerilweng mme o hakanye tlhoko ya yona ho tswa ditlalehong tsa hao. Bapisa seo le phepelo ho pholletsa le dihla.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Ngola intended uses mme o hakanye demand ya tsona o sebedisa records tsa hao. Bapisa phepelo le ditshebediso tseo ho pholletsa le dihla.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Rala seo o tla se etsa ha metsi a bolokilweng a qala ho fela. Lebitso la provense feela le ke ke la o jwetsa boholo ba tanka eo o e hlokang.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Rala seo o tla se etsa ha metsi a bolokilweng a fokotseha. Lebitso la provense feela ha le bolele boholo ba tank boo o bo hlokang.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Boloka tanka e kwahetswe, screen openings against insects, mme o hlokomele marulelo, dikoto le sekgelo (diverter). Boloka metsi a pula a arohane le diphaephe tsa metsi a nowang.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Kwahela tank, kwahela masoba ka mesh e thibelang dikokonyana, mme o hlokomele marulelo, gutters le diverter. Arola metsi a pula le diphaephe tsa drinking water.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka diteko le kalafo tse loketseng tshebediso e rerilweng.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Metsi a shebahalang a hlakile a ntse a ka ba le germs kapa chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka testing le treatment tse loketseng intended use.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Metsi a sebedisitsweng a lapeng a ka ba le dikokwana-hloko, matswai, dihlahiswa tsa ho hlwekisa le dintho tse ding. Ditaelo ha di hlalose mohlodi o mong le o mong ka mokgwa o tshwanang. Ditaelo tsa Afrika Borwa di fapana mabapi le kitchen water le laundry water.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Metsi a sebedisitsweng ka lapeng a ka ba le germs, salts, cleaning products le dintho tse ding. Ditaelo ha di hlalose mohlodi o mong le o mong ka tsela e tshwanang. Ditaelo tsa Afrika Borwa di fapana mabapi le kitchen water le laundry water.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: O se ke wa kenya toilet water, water from nappies, a ho hlatswa motho ya kulang kapa a ho hlatswa diphoofolo moralong wa reuse. O se ke wa sebedisa hape metsi a nang le harmful chemicals.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Pele ho reuse efe kapa efe, kopa municipality le qualified local sanitation adviser hore ba hlahlobe source e tobileng, ditshebeletso tsa metsi le sanitation tsa household, intended use le site. Haeba keletso ena e sa fumanehe kapa e sa hlaka, o se ke wa sebedisa metsi hape.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Setshwantsho se akaretsang ha se moralo wa polasi. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Setshwantsho se akaretsang hase farm design. Soil le mulch ha di disinfect wastewater. Boloka wastewater hole le drinking-water plumbing mme o thibele ho kopana ha yona le batho kapa diphoofolo. O se ke wa e fafatsa, wa e tlohela e eme, kapa wa dumella hore e phalle kantle ho property ho kena seterateng, drain kapa watercourse.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Haeba reuse system e se e sebetsa and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, emisa ho e sebedisa mme seek qualified local advice.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Haeba reuse system e se e sebetsa mme metsi a nkha hampe, a etsa letamo kapa a senya dimela, emisa ho a sebedisa mme o batle keletso ho qualified local adviser.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.
changedSegments.currentSegment: One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. I fhungudza luvhilo na u phaḓaladza runoff, uri maḓi maṅwe a kone u dzhena kha suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Lushaka luthihi lwa swale ndi a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Nḓila ine ya fanelea shango ḽaṋu i bva kha soil, slope, drainage na storm flow. Musi ni sa athu u bwa, humbelani trained local adviser uri a sedze line, overflow na receiving point.
changedSegments.amendmentReason: High-risk construction geometry is source-exact for level trench on contour, controlled grade, excess water, safe outlet, line, overflow, receiving point and before-digging assessment. Ordinary land-fit explanation and local adviser framing remain localized; no long trench is added.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Mavu o excavated a vhumba berm on the downhill side, hune trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Mavu o excavated a vhumba berm nga thungo ya le downhill, hune miri ya nga ṱavhiwa arali site design yo tea.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Miri yo ṱavhiwaho henefho may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Miri yo ṱavhiwaho henefho i nga shumisa moisture yo vhulungwaho mavuni nga murahu ha mvula, zwi tshi ya nga site.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Pula khulwane i nga ḓadza swale nga u ṱavhanya u fhira u dzhena ha maḓi mavuni. Plan a safe overflow before digging.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Pulani safe overflow ni sa athu u bwa.
changedSegments.amendmentReason: Uses exact source term “Heavy rain” because “Pula” may be Sesotho contamination; keeps the existing Tshivenda before-digging overflow instruction.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Route a i tei u erode slope kana u rumela damaging water kha neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Route a i tei u erode slope kana u rumela damaging water kha neighbour. Swale kana dam ya fhasi i tea u kona u ṱanganedza maḓi ayo nga vhuḓi.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. Tshifanyiso a si construction design.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Humbelani trained local adviser uri a assess soil, slope na storm flow. Tshifanyiso a si construction design.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Keep good ground cover. Wanani local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers na terraces na zwone zwi ṱoḓa a design suited to the site.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Keep good ground cover. Wanani local assessment ni sa athu u bwa kha fhethu ha steep, wet kana unstable. Grass barriers na terraces na zwone zwi ṱoḓa design yo teaho site.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Dam kana pond i nga vhulunga runoff, fhedzi amount i re hone i bva kha local rain, catchment, losses na uri ni shumisa maḓi mangana.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Dam kana pond i nga vhulunga runoff, fhedzi maḓi ane a wanala a bva kha mvula ya henefho, catchment, losses na uri ni shumisa maḓi mangana.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Tshifhinga tsha mvula tshi a fhambana u mona na Afurika Tshipembe. Shumisani local records ni pulanele dry periods; dam yo ḓalaho a yo khwaṱhisedzwi.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Tshifhinga tsha mvula tshi a fhambana u mona na Afurika Tshipembe. Shumisani local records nahone ni pulanele dry periods; dam yo ḓalaho a yo khwaṱhisedzwi.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Musi ni sa athu shandula watercourse kana u fhaṱa storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Musi ni sa athu u shandula watercourse kana u fhaṱa storage works, ṱolani authorisation ine ya ṱoḓea kha water authority.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Overflow i songo langiwaho i nga erode na breach wall. Plan safe route ya excess water before construction.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Overflow i songo langiwaho i nga erode na breach wall. Pulani safe route ya excess water ni sa athu u thoma construction.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Maḓi a nga xela nga evaporation na seepage. Check water level ni sedze leaks kana erosion.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Maḓi a nga xela nga evaporation na seepage. Sedzani water level, ni ṱole leaks kana erosion.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Keep spillway i clear nahone maintain bank cover yo bulwaho kha design. Do not plant trees on earth dam wall.
changedSegments.proposedSegment: Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Ni songo ṱavha trees kha earth dam wall.
changedSegments.amendmentReason: The earlier “Hlayisani” is flagged as wrong-language contamination. Preserve exact English for clear spillway and designed bank-cover requirements; retain localized prohibition.

changedSegments.sourceParagraph: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
changedSegments.currentSegment: Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. U vha hone hazwi iti uri maḓi a vhe clean kana safe.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
sourceCandidateHistory.currentTarget:
Mofuta o mong wa swale ke level trench on contour. E fokotsa lebelo mme e hasanya runoff, hore metsi a mang a kgone ho kenella mobung o loketseng. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Mokgwa o loketseng naha ya hao o itshetlehile ka mobu, slope, drainage le storm flow. Pele o tjheka, trained local adviser a hlahlobe line, overflow le receiving point.

Mobu o epolotsweng o etsa berm on the downhill side; moo difate di ka jalwang ha site design e loketse.

Difate tse jetsweng moo di ka nka moisture e bolokilweng mobung ka mora pula, ho ya ka site.

Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rera safe overflow pele o tjheka.

Route eo ha e a tshwanela ho senya slope ka erosion kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. Downstream swale kapa dam e lokela ho kgona ho amohela metsi ao ka polokeho.

Kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe mobu, slope le storm flow. Setshwantsho ha se construction design.

Slope feela ha e bolele hore swale e a lokela. Soil, drainage, unstable ground le metsi a tswang upslope kaofela di bohlokwa.

Boloka ground cover e ntle. Fumana local assessment pele o tjheka mobung o steep, wet kapa unstable. Grass barriers le terraces le tsona di hloka design e loketseng site.

segments.proposedSegment: Mobu o epolotsweng o etsa berm ka lehlakoreng le theohelang, moo difate di ka jalwang teng ha site design e loketse.

segments.sourceParagraph: Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.
segments.currentSegment: Difate tse jetsweng moo di ka nka moisture e bolokilweng mobung ka mora pula, ho ya ka site.
segments.proposedSegment: Difate tse jalwang moo di ka sebedisa metsi a bolokilweng mobung ka mora pula, ho ya ka site.

segments.sourceParagraph: Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.
segments.currentSegment: Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rera safe overflow pele o tjheka.
segments.proposedSegment: Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rala tsela e bolokehileng ya overflow pele o tjheka.

segments.sourceParagraph: The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.
segments.currentSegment: Route eo ha e a tshwanela ho senya slope ka erosion kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. Downstream swale kapa dam e lokela ho kgona ho amohela metsi ao ka polokeho.
segments.proposedSegment: Tsela ha e a lokela ho baka erosion moepeng kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. Swale kapa dam e tlase e lokela ho kgona ho amohela metsi ao ka polokeho.

segments.sourceParagraph: Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.
segments.currentSegment: Kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe mobu, slope le storm flow. Setshwantsho ha se construction design.
segments.proposedSegment: Kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe mobu, slope le storm flow. Setshwantsho hase construction design.

segments.sourceParagraph: Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.
segments.currentSegment: Slope feela ha e bolele hore swale e a lokela. Soil, drainage, unstable ground le metsi a tswang upslope kaofela di bohlokwa.
segments.proposedSegment: Slope feela ha e bolele hore swale e loketse. Soil, drainage, unstable ground le metsi a tswang upslope kaofela di bohlokwa.

segments.sourceParagraph: Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
segments.currentSegment: Boloka ground cover e ntle. Fumana local assessment pele o tjheka mobung o steep, wet kapa unstable. Grass barriers le terraces le tsona di hloka design e loketseng site.
segments.proposedSegment: Boloka ground cover e ntle. Fumana local assessment pele o tjheka sebakeng se steep, wet kapa unstable. Grass barriers le terraces le tsona di hloka design e loketseng site.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.
sourceCandidateHistory.currentTarget:
Letamo kapa letangwana le ka boloka metsi a phallang, empa bongata bo fumanehang bo itshetlehile ka pula ya sebaka seo, sebaka se kgoboketsang metsi (catchment), tahlehelo le hore na o sebedisa metsi a makae.

Dihla tsa pula di fapana ho pholletsa le Afrika Borwa (South Africa). Sebedisa ditlaleho tsa sebaka seo mme o rale bakeng sa dry periods; letamo le tletseng ha le a tiisetswa.

Pele o fetola tsela ya noka kapa molatswana (watercourse) kapa o haha meaho ya polokelo, hlahloba tumello e hlokahalang le balaodi ba metsi.

Letamo le hloka dipatlisiso tsa setsha le moralo o entsweng ke motho ya nang le ditshwaneleho tse loketseng. Metsi a phallang ho tswa sebakeng sa pokellelo (catchment runoff), mobu, metheo, kotsi e ka tlase (downstream risk) le tsela e bolokehileng ya metsi a tletseng (safe spillway) kaofela a bohlokwa.

O se ke wa nka hore pula ya selemo le selemo e o jwetsa boholo ba morwallo kapa polokelo eo o tla ba le yona.

Phallo e sa laolweng ya metsi a tletseng e ka kgohola le ho pshatla lerako. Rala tsela e bolokehileng bakeng sa metsi a feteletseng pele ho kaho.

Metsi a ka lahleha ka evaporation and seepage. Hlahloba boemo ba metsi mme o batle dibaka tse dutlang kapa kgoholeho.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. O se ke wa jala difate hodima lerako la letamo la mobu.

Diphoofolo di ka senya mabopo mme tsa eketsa mantle ka hara metsi. Ho ba teng ha tsona ha ho etse hore metsi a hlweke kapa a bolokehe.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.

Marulelo a hao a ka bokella metsi a pula. Bongata bo itshetlehile ka boholo ba marulelo, pula le tahlehelo.

Hlahloba hore na thepa ya marulelo e loketse ho bokella metsi a pula pele o hokela tanka.

Sebedisa boholo ba marulelo jwalo ka ha bo bonwa ho tloha hodimo le ditlaleho tsa pula ya sebaka seo. Ebe o dumella metsi a fosang koto, a kgelohang kapa a kgaphatsehang ha tanka e tletse.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Bapisa phepelo le tshebediso eo o e rerileng.

Metsi a theohang marulelong a ka nka lerole, mantle le tshilafalo e nngwe. Sekgelo sa ho qala ha phallo (first-flush diverter) se boloka karolo e nngwe ya metsi a pele a phallang kantle ho tanka.

Bongata bo hlokahalang ba ho kgeloha bo itshetlehile ka marulelo le tsamaiso. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

Sekgelo (diverter) ha se etse hore metsi a setseng a bolokehele ho nowa.

Boholo ba tanka bo itshetlehile ka tlhoko ya metsi, pula, boholo ba marulelo le the length of dry periods.

Ngola tshebediso e rerilweng mme o hakanye tlhoko ya yona ho tswa ditlalehong tsa hao. Bapisa seo le phepelo ho pholletsa le dihla.

Rala seo o tla se etsa ha metsi a bolokilweng a qala ho fela. Lebitso la provense feela le ke ke la o jwetsa boholo ba tanka eo o e hlokang.

Boloka tanka e kwahetswe, screen openings against insects, mme o hlokomele marulelo, dikoto le sekgelo (diverter). Boloka metsi a pula a arohane le diphaephe tsa metsi a nowang.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka diteko le kalafo tse loketseng tshebediso e rerilweng.

Sefa sa mantlha feela hase tiiso ya metsi a nowang. Metsi a sebediswang dijalong tsa dijo le ona a hloka tlhahlobo ya polokeho.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.

One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.

Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.
sourceCandidateHistory.currentTarget:
Muxaka wun'we wa xisele (swale) i mugodi wo leha lowu ringaneke, lowu celiweke eka khanthura. Wu nonokisa mati lama khulukaka (runoff) wu tlhela wu ma hangalasa, so some water can soak into suitable soil. Swisele swin'wana swi dizayiniwa swi rhelela katsongo hi ndlela leyi lawulekaka, leswaku swi yisa mati lama taleke hi ku nonoka eka ndhawu leyi hlayisekeke yo huma. Ndlela leyi faneleke ndhawu ya wena yi titshege hi misava, ku rhelela, ku humesa mati na ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze. Kombela mutsundzuxi wa laha kaya loyi a leteriweke leswaku a kambela layini, ndlela ya mati lama taleke na ndhawu leyi ma yaka kona u nga si cela.

Misava leyi celiweke yi endla khurhana ra misava (berm) etlhelweni ra le hansi, laha mirhi yi nga byariwaka kona loko dizayini ya ndhawu yi fanerile.

Mirhi leyi byariweke kona yi nga tirhisa ku tsakama loku hlayisiweke emisaveni endzhaku ka mpfula, swi ya hi ndhawu.

Mpfula ya matimba yi nga tata xisele hi ku hatlisa ku tlula hilaha mati ma nghenaka hakona emisaveni. Kunguhatela ndlela leyi hlayisekeke ya mati lama taleke u nga si cela.

Ndlela ya kona a yi fanelanga ku kukula misava ya ndhawu yo rhelela kumbe ku rhumela mati lama onhaka eka muakelani. Xisele kumbe damu leri nga ehansi swi fanele ku kota ku ma amukela hi vuhlayiseki.

Kombela mutsundzuxi wa laha kaya loyi a leteriweke leswaku a kambela misava, ku rhelela na ku khuluka ka mati ya xidzedze. Xifaniso a hi dizayini yo aka ha yona.

Ku rhelela ntsena a ku ku byeli loko xisele xi fanerile. Misava, ku humesa mati, misava leyi nga tiyangiki na mati lama taka hi le henhla ka ndhawu yo rhelela hinkwaswo swa nkoka.

Hlayisa misava yi funengetekile kahle. Kuma nkambelo wa laha kaya u nga si cela eka steep, wet or unstable land. Mindzilakano ya byanyi (grass barriers) na titerasi (terraces) na swona swi lava dizayini leyi faneleke ndhawu.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.

sourceCandidateHistory.source:
Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.

Xifaniso xa ntolovelo a hi pulani ya purasi. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

U nga katsi mati ya toilet, mati yo huma eka nappies, mati yo hlantswa munhu loyi a vabyaka kumbe mati yo hlantswa swiharhi eka reuse plan. U nga tirhisi nakambe mati lama nga na harmful chemicals.

U nga ma fafazeli, u ma tshiki ma yima, kumbe u pfumelela ma khulukela ehandle ka property ku ya exitarateni, drain kumbe watercourse.

verifiedCandidateFields.sourceEnglish:
One kind of swale is a level trench on contour. It slows and spreads runoff so some water can soak into suitable soil. Other swales are designed with a slight, controlled grade to carry excess water slowly to a safe outlet. Which approach fits your land depends on the soil, slope, drainage and storm flow. Have a trained local adviser check the line, overflow and receiving point before digging.

The excavated soil forms a berm on the downhill side, where trees can be planted when the site design is suitable.

Trees planted there may draw on moisture stored in the soil after rain, depending on the site.

Heavy rain can fill a swale faster than water soaks into the soil. Plan a safe overflow before digging.

The route must not erode the slope or send damaging water to a neighbour. A downstream swale or dam must be able to receive it safely.

Ask a trained local adviser to assess the soil, slope and storm flow. A picture is not a construction design.

Slope alone does not tell you whether a swale is suitable. Soil, drainage, unstable ground and the water arriving from upslope all matter.

Keep good ground cover. Get a local assessment before digging on steep, wet or unstable land. Grass barriers and terraces also need a design suited to the site.

Pele o tjheka, trained local adviser a hlahlobe line, overflow le receiving point.

Mobu o epolotsweng o etsa berm on the downhill side; moo difate di ka jalwang ha site design e loketse.

Difate tse jetsweng moo di ka nka moisture e bolokilweng mobung ka mora pula, ho ya ka site.

Pula e matla e ka tlatsa swale ka potlako ho feta kamoo metsi a kenellang mobung. Rera safe overflow pele o tjheka.

Route eo ha e a tshwanela ho senya slope ka erosion kapa ho romela metsi a senyang ho moahisani. Downstream swale kapa dam e lokela ho kgona ho amohela metsi ao ka polokeho.

Kopa trained local adviser hore a hlahlobe mobu, slope le storm flow. Setshwantsho ha se construction design.

Slope feela ha e bolele hore swale e a lokela. Soil, drainage, unstable ground le metsi a tswang upslope kaofela di bohlokwa.

Boloka ground cover e ntle. Fumana local assessment pele o tjheka mobung o steep, wet kapa unstable. Grass barriers le terraces le tsona di hloka design e loketseng site.

verifiedCandidateFields.sourceEnglish:
A dam or pond can store runoff, but the amount available depends on local rain, the catchment, losses and how much water you use.

Rainfall seasons differ across South Africa. Use local records and plan for dry periods; a full dam is not guaranteed.

Before changing a watercourse or building storage works, check the required authorisation with the water authority.

A dam needs a site investigation and a design by a suitably qualified person. Catchment runoff, soil, foundations, downstream risk and a safe spillway all matter.

Do not assume that annual rainfall tells you the size of a flood or the storage you will have.

An uncontrolled overflow can erode and breach the wall. Plan a safe route for excess water before construction.

Water can be lost through evaporation and seepage. Check the water level and look for leaks or erosion.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. Do not plant trees on an earth dam wall.

Animals can damage banks and add manure to the water. Their presence does not make the water clean or safe.

Letamo kapa letangwana le ka boloka metsi a phallang, empa bongata bo fumanehang bo itshetlehile ka pula ya sebaka seo, sebaka se kgoboketsang metsi (catchment), tahlehelo le hore na o sebedisa metsi a makae.

Dihla tsa pula di fapana ho pholletsa le Afrika Borwa (South Africa). Sebedisa ditlaleho tsa sebaka seo mme o rale bakeng sa dry periods; letamo le tletseng ha le a tiisetswa.

Pele o fetola tsela ya noka kapa molatswana (watercourse) kapa o haha meaho ya polokelo, hlahloba tumello e hlokahalang le balaodi ba metsi.

Letamo le hloka dipatlisiso tsa setsha le moralo o entsweng ke motho ya nang le ditshwaneleho tse loketseng. Metsi a phallang ho tswa sebakeng sa pokellelo (catchment runoff), mobu, metheo, kotsi e ka tlase (downstream risk) le tsela e bolokehileng ya metsi a tletseng (safe spillway) kaofela a bohlokwa.

O se ke wa nka hore pula ya selemo le selemo e o jwetsa boholo ba morwallo kapa polokelo eo o tla ba le yona.

Phallo e sa laolweng ya metsi a tletseng e ka kgohola le ho pshatla lerako. Rala tsela e bolokehileng bakeng sa metsi a feteletseng pele ho kaho.

Metsi a ka lahleha ka evaporation and seepage. Hlahloba boemo ba metsi mme o batle dibaka tse dutlang kapa kgoholeho.

Keep the spillway clear and maintain the bank cover specified in the design. O se ke wa jala difate hodima lerako la letamo la mobu.

Diphoofolo di ka senya mabopo mme tsa eketsa mantle ka hara metsi. Ho ba teng ha tsona ha ho etse hore metsi a hlweke kapa a bolokehe.

verifiedCandidateFields.sourceEnglish:
Your roof can collect rainwater. The amount depends on roof area, rainfall and losses.

Check whether the roof material is suitable for rainwater collection before connecting a tank.

Use the roof area seen from above and local rainfall records. Then allow for water that misses the gutter, is diverted or overflows a full tank.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Compare supply with the uses you plan.

Roof runoff can carry dust, droppings and other contamination. A first-flush diverter keeps some of the first runoff out of the tank.

The required diversion depends on the roof and system. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

A diverter does not make the remaining water safe to drink.

Tank size depends on water demand, rain, roof area and the length of dry periods.

List the intended uses and estimate their demand from your own records. Compare that with supply through the seasons.

Plan what you will do when stored water runs low. A province name alone cannot tell you the tank size you need.

Keep the tank covered, screen openings against insects, and maintain the roof, gutters and diverter. Keep rainwater separate from drinking-water pipes.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.

A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
verifiedCandidateFields.currentTarget:
Marulelo a hao a ka bokella metsi a pula. Bongata bo itshetlehile ka boholo ba marulelo, pula le tahlehelo.

Hlahloba hore na thepa ya marulelo e loketse ho bokella metsi a pula pele o hokela tanka.

Sebedisa boholo ba marulelo jwalo ka ha bo bonwa ho tloha hodimo le ditlaleho tsa pula ya sebaka seo. Ebe o dumella metsi a fosang koto, a kgelohang kapa a kgaphatsehang ha tanka e tletse.

An annual total does not tell you how much water will be available during a dry spell. Bapisa phepelo le tshebediso eo o e rerileng.

Metsi a theohang marulelong a ka nka lerole, mantle le tshilafalo e nngwe. Sekgelo sa ho qala ha phallo (first-flush diverter) se boloka karolo e nngwe ya metsi a pele a phallang kantle ho tanka.

Bongata bo hlokahalang ba ho kgeloha bo itshetlehile ka marulelo le tsamaiso. Use the supplier's sizing and maintenance instructions; there is no single volume for every roof.

Sekgelo (diverter) ha se etse hore metsi a setseng a bolokehele ho nowa.

Boholo ba tanka bo itshetlehile ka tlhoko ya metsi, pula, boholo ba marulelo le the length of dry periods.

Ngola tshebediso e rerilweng mme o hakanye tlhoko ya yona ho tswa ditlalehong tsa hao. Bapisa seo le phepelo ho pholletsa le dihla.

Rala seo o tla se etsa ha metsi a bolokilweng a qala ho fela. Lebitso la provense feela le ke ke la o jwetsa boholo ba tanka eo o e hlokang.

Boloka tanka e kwahetswe, screen openings against insects, mme o hlokomele marulelo, dikoto le sekgelo (diverter). Boloka metsi a pula a arohane le diphaephe tsa metsi a nowang.

Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka diteko le kalafo tse loketseng tshebediso e rerilweng.

Sefa sa mantlha feela hase tiiso ya metsi a nowang. Metsi a sebediswang dijalong tsa dijo le ona a hloka tlhahlobo ya polokeho.

paragraphComposition.proposedParagraph: Kwahela tank, kwahela masoba ka mesh e thibelang dikokonyana, mme o hlokomele marulelo, gutters le diverter. Arola metsi a pula le diphaephe tsa drinking water.

paragraphComposition.sourceParagraph: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Ask the local health authority about testing and treatment suited to the intended use.
paragraphComposition.currentParagraph: Water that looks clear may still contain germs or chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka diteko le kalafo tse loketseng tshebediso e rerilweng.
paragraphComposition.proposedParagraph: Metsi a shebahalang a hlakile a ntse a ka ba le germs kapa chemicals. Botsa balaodi ba bophelo bo botle ba sebaka seo ka testing le treatment tse loketseng intended use.

paragraphComposition.sourceParagraph: A basic filter alone is not a drinking-water guarantee. Water used on food crops also needs a safety assessment.
paragraphComposition.currentParagraph: Sefa sa mantlha feela hase tiiso ya metsi a nowang. Metsi a sebediswang dijalong tsa dijo le ona a hloka tlhahlobo ya polokeho.
paragraphComposition.proposedParagraph: Sefa sa mantlha feela hase tiiso ya metsi a nowang. Metsi a sebediswang dijalong tsa dijo le ona a hloka tlhahlobo ya polokeho.

Used household water can contain germs, salts, cleaning products and other substances. Guidance does not define every source in the same way. South African guidance differs on kitchen water and laundry water.

Do not include toilet water, water from nappies, washing a sick person or washing animals in a reuse plan. Do not reuse water containing harmful chemicals.

Before any reuse, ask the municipality and a qualified local sanitation adviser to check the exact source, the household's water and sanitation services, the intended use and the site. If this advice is unavailable or unclear, do not reuse the water.

A generic picture is not a farm design. Soil and mulch do not disinfect wastewater. Keep it away from drinking-water plumbing and prevent contact with people or animals. Do not spray it, let it pool, or allow it to run off the property into a street, drain or watercourse.

If a reuse system is already operating and the water smells bad, pools or harms plants, stop using it and seek qualified local advice.
